question: Can two further public representations complement the four members actually elected in the previous run? Does the ordinary solver make a useful different choice when both become available?
audition: Reuse the frozen four-member election, actual fitted components, exact group roles and worker payload of the resource audition. Both newly declared encoders receive one identical opportunity to fit the existing generic classification head. Precompute only frozen, label-free vectors for fitting and nomination titles, using their own published pooling rules. Accumulate counts for the protected baseline, each new resource, and their uniform combination, with total new weights 25%, 50% or 100%. On the nomination set choose highest accuracy, then less total new weight, fewer new models, then content ID. A tie with the incumbent retains it. Lock the full choice before examining a further role. A nonzero choice must improve strictly on both subsequent group-disjoint roles before promotion. Stop on the first nonpositive check. Never reselect on these checks.
ordinary: Offer all installed candidates including the two additions to the same anonymized ordinary entry, with 32 actual fits and 1800s, and reuse the corresponding previous control and immutable training and query packets. No names, advice or weights enter the solver. Its selected models and row predictions are sealed before comparison with the development answers. Record exposure, exploration and winning membership separately. Treat any gain on this previously studied partition as development evidence.
budget: Two supervised fits for the matched audition and up to 32 for the independent ordinary run. Frozen inference is reported separately. No model service, course-designated validation labels, official test data or H2.
